disclaimer: Gene functions derived from published databases and peer-reviewed literature. Sorghum bicolor has a well-annotated reference genome (BTx623, JGI Phytozome v3.1). Entries represent characterized or well-supported homolog-based assignments. Expression under Texas field conditions requires experimental validation.

evidenceLevelKey.Peer-Reviewed Literature: Gene directly characterized in Sorghum bicolor in a published peer-reviewed study.
evidenceLevelKey.Curated Database Reference: Gene annotated in a curated database (Phytozome, Gramene, KEGG) for Sorghum bicolor.
evidenceLevelKey.Homology-Based Projection: Gene inferred from well-characterized ortholog in maize, Arabidopsis, or rice.
evidenceLevelKey.Environment-Relevance Estimate: Pathway relevance inferred from environmental conditions and sorghum stress physiology literature.

genes.name: Cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase 2
genes.functionSummary: Catalyzes the final step of monolignol biosynthesis — reduction of cinnamaldehydes to cinnamyl alcohols (coniferyl, sinapyl, p-coumaryl alcohol). The brown midrib (bmr) sorghum lines with reduced SbCAD activity show lower lignin and improved cell wall digestibility for ethanol production.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbCAD2 (Sobic.004G163400); Saballos A et al. 2008 Genetics 181(2):783–795
genes.limitationNote: Well-characterized in bmr sorghum lines. Multiple CAD paralogs exist; SbCAD2 is the primary lignin-associated isoform.

genes.name: Caffeic acid O-methyltransferase (BMR12 locus)
genes.functionSummary: Methylates caffeic acid and 5-hydroxyferulic acid in the monolignol pathway. The bmr12 sorghum mutant (reduced SbCoMT) shows drastically reduced syringyl (S) lignin, lower total lignin, and substantially improved bioenergy digestibility and cellulosic ethanol yield.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbCoMT (Sobic.009G174200); Bout S, Vermerris W 2003 Mol Genet Genomics 269(2):205–214
genes.limitationNote: One of the most studied sorghum bioenergy genes. Field validation under Texas summer heat conditions adds confidence.

genes.name: Caffeoyl-CoA O-methyltransferase
genes.functionSummary: Methylates caffeoyl-CoA in the guaiacyl (G) lignin biosynthetic branch. Acts upstream of SbCoMT. Contributes to overall lignin density in vascular tissue and stem internodes.
genes.orthologSource: Maize ZmCCoAOMT1 ortholog; Sobic.007G074600 (Phytozome); Do CT et al. 2007 Phytochemistry 68(14):1958–1988
genes.limitationNote: Multiple paralogs; gene identity confirmed by Phytozome annotation.

genes.name: Cellulose synthase catalytic subunit 7
genes.functionSummary: Core catalytic subunit of the cellulose synthase complex (CSC) involved in secondary cell wall cellulose deposition in stems and vascular tissue. Cellulose content directly determines ethanol yield potential from cellulosic conversion pathways.
genes.orthologSource: Maize ZmCesA10/IRX3 ortholog; Sobic.001G399700 (Phytozome); Kumar M et al. 2016 Plant Cell 28(3):574–596
genes.limitationNote: CesA family has 10+ members in sorghum; CesA7 is the secondary wall isoform most directly tied to biomass cellulose content.

genes.name: Dehydrin 1 (Group 3 LEA protein)
genes.functionSummary: Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) protein expressed strongly under drought, ABA, and cold stress. Dehydrins protect cellular membranes and proteins from dehydration damage by acting as molecular chaperones and preventing protein aggregation.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbDhn1 (Sobic.010G185800); Iskandar HM et al. 2011 BMC Plant Biol 11:141
genes.limitationNote: Sorghum is the most drought-tolerant cereal — dehydrin expression is one of the well-documented drought adaptation mechanisms.

genes.name: Δ1-Pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthetase
genes.functionSummary: Rate-limiting enzyme in proline biosynthesis. Under drought and heat stress, proline accumulates as a compatible solute, providing osmotic adjustment, scavenging reactive oxygen species, and stabilizing membranes and proteins.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbP5CS (Sobic.003G419500); Reddy PS et al. 2015 Sci Rep 5:18311
genes.limitationNote: Proline accumulation under drought is well-documented in sorghum field studies in semi-arid environments.

genes.name: Heat shock protein 90
genes.functionSummary: Major molecular chaperone induced rapidly by heat stress. Prevents misfolding and aggregation of client proteins including transcription factors, signal transducers, and membrane proteins. HSP90 is central to thermotolerance in sorghum.
genes.orthologSource: Maize ZmHSP90 / Arabidopsis AtHSP90.2; Sobic.001G070100 (Phytozome); Djanaguiraman M et al. 2014 J Plant Physiol 171(18):1726–1735
genes.limitationNote: Heat response well-documented in sorghum; key gene for explaining Texas summer performance.

genes.name: Heat shock transcription factor A2
genes.functionSummary: Master regulator of the heat shock transcriptional response. Activates expression of HSP genes by binding heat shock elements (HSEs) in their promoters. HSFA2 is a key coordinator of acquired thermotolerance.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtHSFA2 (AT2G26150); Ohama N et al. 2017 Plant Cell 29(11):2733–2749
genes.limitationNote: Projected from Arabidopsis ortholog; sorghum-specific HSFA2 expression under field heat requires RNA-seq confirmation.

genes.name: Sucrose phosphate synthase 1
genes.functionSummary: Key enzyme in sucrose synthesis, catalyzing the formation of sucrose-6-phosphate from UDP-glucose and fructose-6-phosphate. In sweet sorghum, high SPS activity drives juice sucrose accumulation — the primary fermentable substrate for first-generation bioethanol.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbSPS1 (Sobic.002G256300); Bihmidine S et al. 2015 Plant Physiol 167(4):1523–1534
genes.limitationNote: Sweet sorghum vs. biomass sorghum varieties differ greatly in SPS expression and stem sucrose content.

genes.name: Cytochrome P450 79A1 (dhurrin pathway)
genes.functionSummary: Encodes the first dedicated enzyme in dhurrin (cyanogenic glucoside) biosynthesis in sorghum. Dhurrin accumulates in seedlings and young tissue as a defense compound. Under hydrolysis, it releases HCN (hydrogen cyanide), which can inhibit anaerobic digestion and fermentation microbes — a bioenergy processing concern.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbCYP79A1 (Sobic.007G098400); Busk PK, Møller BL 2002 Plant Physiol 129(3):1253–1262
genes.limitationNote: Dhurrin is highest in young tissues and declines with maturity. Harvesting at physiological maturity greatly reduces HCN risk.

genes.name: Granule-bound starch synthase (Waxy locus)
genes.functionSummary: Controls amylose vs. amylopectin ratio in grain starch. Waxy (null) sorghum genotypes produce all-amylopectin grain starch, which gelatinizes at lower temperatures — reducing energy input for grain-to-ethanol conversion. Relevant to grain sorghum ethanol.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbGBSSI (Sobic.010G271500); Pedersen JF et al. 2000 Crop Sci 40(5):1255–1259
genes.limitationNote: Waxy sorghum varieties are commercially available and used in dry-mill ethanol facilities.

genes.name: Dehydration-responsive element binding protein 2
genes.functionSummary: AP2/ERF-class transcription factor activated by drought and heat stress. Binds drought-responsive elements (DREs) in the promoters of stress-protective genes including dehydrins, late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins, and osmotic stress enzymes.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbDREB2 (Sobic.003G095300); Suárez-López P et al. 2001; Kidokoro S et al. 2017 Plant J 92(4):679–693
genes.limitationNote: DREB2 class is consistently upregulated in drought-stressed sorghum in multiple transcriptomic studies.

genes.name: Ethylene response factor 1
genes.functionSummary: Ethylene response factor transcription factor involved in integrating multiple stress signals (drought, flooding, wounding). ERFs coordinate ethylene-mediated acclimation including aerenchyma formation under waterlogging and senescence acceleration.
genes.orthologSource: Maize ZmERF3 ortholog; Sobic.001G082200 (Phytozome); Müller M, Munné-Bosch S 2015 Plant Cell Environ 38(2):289–302
genes.limitationNote: ERF family is large and complex; specific isoform roles in sorghum stress responses need further characterization.

genes.name: Pyruvate orthophosphate dikinase (C4 carbon concentrating)
genes.functionSummary: Regenerates phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) in mesophyll cells — the CO2 acceptor molecule for C4 carbon fixation. PPDK activity is the primary limiting step in C4 photosynthesis at low temperatures. High PPDK expression is a hallmark of C4 plants like sorghum with high light-use efficiency.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbPPDK (Sobic.002G172300); Leegood RC 2002 New Phytol 154(2):337–352
genes.limitationNote: C4 photosynthesis mechanism is extremely well-characterized in sorghum and maize. Cold sensitivity is a known limitation.

genes.name: Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (C4 primary CO2 capture)
genes.functionSummary: Captures atmospheric CO2 in mesophyll cells by carboxylating PEP to form oxaloacetate, which is then reduced to malate for transport to bundle sheath cells where Rubisco operates in a high-CO2 environment. C4 PEPC is one of the most highly expressed enzymes in sorghum leaves.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbPPC (Sobic.003G156800); Lepiniec L et al. 1994 Plant Mol Biol 26(3):905–916
genes.limitationNote: C4-specific PEPC is well-characterized; sorghum uses the NADP-malic enzyme subtype of C4 photosynthesis.

genes.name: NAC domain transcription factor 45
genes.functionSummary: NAC transcription factor involved in regulation of secondary cell wall biosynthesis. Homologs in Arabidopsis (VND6, NST1/3, SND1) are master regulators of secondary wall deposition including cellulose, lignin, and hemicellulose. Critical target for improving biomass quality via biotechnology.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtNST1 (AT2G46770) / AtSND1 (AT1G32770); Nakano Y et al. 2015 Plant Cell 27(8):2085–2101
genes.limitationNote: NAC TF family is very large; specific sorghum NACs regulating secondary wall biosynthesis need confirmation by gene knockdown.

genes.name: MADS-box flowering time regulator / Maturity locus 1
genes.functionSummary: Controls flowering time in sorghum (Ma1 maturity locus). Late-flowering (stay-green) sorghum varieties redirect resources from grain filling to vegetative biomass, maximizing stem and leaf biomass for cellulosic conversion. Tropical varieties with dominant Ma1 allele are photoperiod-sensitive and don't flower under Texas daylengths — maximizing biomass.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor Ma1/SbSbPRR37 (Sobic.006G057866); Murphy RL et al. 2011 Genetics 189(1):341–351
genes.limitationNote: Ma1–Ma4 maturity loci are among the most important genes for energy sorghum variety selection in Texas.

genes.name: Responsive-to-desiccation 22 (BURP domain protein)
genes.functionSummary: ABA-induced BURP-domain protein with predicted function in seed storage and drought stress response. RD22 is a classical drought-induced gene identified in Arabidopsis; sorghum orthologs are induced by ABA, drought, and osmotic stress in leaves and roots.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtRD22 (AT5G25610); Yamaguchi-Shinozaki K, Shinozaki K 1993 Mol Gen Genet 236(2-3):331–340
genes.limitationNote: Projection from Arabidopsis ortholog; sorghum ABA-induced gene characterization at transcript level supports this assignment.

genes.name: Laccase 4 (lignin polymerization)
genes.functionSummary: Copper-containing oxidase that polymerizes monolignols into the lignin polymer. Laccases and peroxidases are responsible for the oxidative coupling that forms the mature lignin network in the cell wall. Reducing laccase activity can decrease lignin content.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtLAC4 (AT2G38080); Zhao Q et al. 2013 Plant Cell 25(9):3498–3512
genes.limitationNote: Laccase family has 17+ members in Arabidopsis; LAC4 and LAC17 are the primary lignin-polymerizing isoforms.

genes.name: Manganese superoxide dismutase 1
genes.functionSummary: Mitochondrial Mn-SOD that converts superoxide radicals generated by electron transport chain stress to hydrogen peroxide (subsequently detoxified by catalase). ROS accumulation under heat and drought stress causes membrane lipid peroxidation and protein damage — SOD activity is a key thermotolerance determinant.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum bicolor SbMnSOD (Sobic.002G361500); Gill SS, Tuteja N 2010 Plant Physiol Biochem 48(12):909–930
genes.limitationNote: Antioxidant enzyme systems are well-characterized in sorghum; SOD upregulation under heat/drought is broadly documented.
